content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
Ward is a free, open-source anti-cyberbullying app for children (Hacktoberfest DEV entry, public MIT repo). Its web demo is a Render static site that runs entirely in the visitor's browser (Ward Lite ONNX model + word lists); the optional Gemma demo calls a relay on a separate Render web service. An audit found the site has no security headers; the owner asked for them in a parallel session while the main session runs a DigitalOcean GPU job. The owner prefers committing verified changes straight to main, no branches.

Task:
Add security headers to Ward's live static site on Render (https://ward-w8cd.onrender.com, Render service `srv-dbj3vomc6qcc73bdg33g` in workspace `tea-davp1jm7bikc73etlheg`; the repo is this checkout, `/Users/haider/Desktop/Hacktoberfest 26/ward`, pushed straight to `main`).

Headers to set: a strict Content-Security-Policy that still lets the app work (it loads its own JS, CSS, fonts, the Ward Lite model under `/models/` and ONNX Runtime wasm under `/ort/` — wasm needs `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` in script-src; the web demo POSTs to `https://ward-discord.onrender.com/gemma` and may probe `http://127.0.0.1:11434` for a local Ollama, so connect-src needs `'self'`, that relay, and the localhost Ollama address; check `apps/web/src` for any other fetches, workers, blob: or data: use before finalising), `X-Frame-Options: DENY` plus `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and a restrictive `Permissions-Policy` (camera stays allowed for self, since counsellor mode scans QR codes). The case viewer `/ward-viewer.html` already has its own meta CSP; make sure the site header doesn't break it (it uses inline script and style), e.g. with a path-specific header.

How: the Render MCP connector can't set static-site headers, so add them to `render.yaml` as a `type: web` + `runtime: static` service named `ward` with `headers:` and a SPA rewrite to `/index.html`, matching the live service's build (`corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm --filter @ward/web build`, publish `apps/web/dist`, env `NODE_VERSION=24` and `VITE_GEMMA_DEMO_URL=https://ward-discord.onrender.com/gemma`). Then tell the user exactly how to apply it: Render dashboard → the `ward` static site → Settings → Headers (paste each), or a Blueprint sync — they do that step themselves. Don't touch the `ward-discord` service or anything under `apps/discord`.

Done when: `render.yaml` has the headers, it's committed and pushed to `main` (end the commit message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`), the user has the exact header lines to apply, and after they apply them you've verified with `curl -sI` that the headers are served and loaded the live site in the browser to confirm the app, a chat check, the Ward Lite model and `/ward-viewer.html` still work with no CSP errors in the console.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/haider/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_8543c787-aaef-4c65-89a8-584174a81e72

# Ward's Discord bot as a Render background worker. It holds a gateway connection open, so it
# needs an always-on instance; it serves no web traffic. Set DISCORD_TOKEN and DISCORD_APP_ID in
# the Render dashboard (never in this file). Server mode stays off here: it's a moderator tool
# that needs a safeguarding review before it's offered publicly (docs/SAFEGUARDING.md section 13),
# so this worker runs personal mode only and never asks Discord for message content.

    name: ward-discord
    runtime: node
    plan: starter

    buildCommand: corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter "@ward/discord..."
    startCommand: pnpm --filter @ward/discord start
    envVars:
      - key: NODE_VERSION
        value: "24"
      - key: DISCORD_TOKEN
        sync: false
      - key: DISCORD_APP_ID
        sync: false
      - key: WARD_SERVER_MODE
        value: "off"

content.text:
I added the security headers for the web demo to `render.yaml` and pushed the change to `main` as commit `08e4c69`. They aren't live yet, so I haven't checked them against the site. The live site already sends `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, but none of the others.

**To apply them:** in the Render dashboard, open the **ward** static site → **Settings → Headers** and add these rules:

| Path | Name | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `/*` | `Content-Security-Policy` | `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self' data:; media-src 'self' blob:; connect-src 'self' https://ward-discord.onrender.com http://127.0.0.1:11434 http://localhost:11434; manifest-src 'self'; worker-src 'self' blob:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'` |
| `/ward-viewer.html` | `Content-Security-Policy` | `default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'` |
| `/*` | `X-Frame-Options` | `DENY` |
| `/*` | `Referrer-Policy` | `no-referrer` |
| `/*` | `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` |
| `/*` | `Permissions-Policy` | `camera=(self), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=(), serial=(), bluetooth=(), midi=(), magnetometer=(), gyroscope=(), accelerometer=(), display-capture=(), interest-cohort=()` |

Don't set it up through a Blueprint sync. The live site wasn't created from this file, so a sync could create a second `ward` site instead of updating the current one.

**Three things to know:**
- **The case viewer might still break.** I couldn't confirm what Render does when two rules set the same header on one path. If it sends both, the browser applies both policies, and the site-wide one blocks the viewer's inline script. When I verify, I'll check exactly what `/ward-viewer.html` gets. If both arrive, the fix is to allow the viewer's inline code by its hash in the site-wide policy.
- **Local Ollama only works at the default address.** The policy allows `127.0.0.1:11434` and `localhost:11434`. If a visitor points the app at a different Ollama address, the browser will block it.
- **The `'unsafe-inline'` in `style-src` is a guess.** I allowed inline styles because React components usually set styles inline. I didn't confirm that this app needs it; if the console stays clean without it, it can come out later.

Once you've applied them, I'll check with `curl -sI`. Then I'll load the live site to confirm a chat check, the Ward Lite model and `/ward-viewer.html` still work with no CSP errors in the console.
